_comment: COLLECTION EXHAUSTION — which evidence layers have actually run against a seed, and what each one that has NOT run would have bought. This exists because of a measurable failure: across the stored collections in this repo, `intelx` appears in `enriched_with` exactly ONCE. The leak / stealer-log corpus, passive SSL, Censys and the advertising layer are all opt-in flags, so in practice a case gets the first fetch — the TRIAGE — and then moves on to correlation as though the seed had been worked out. The correlation is then honest about everything except the size of the search it was drawn from, and 'nothing further found' silently means 'nothing further was looked for'. This file is the checklist that makes the difference visible: each layer says how to tell it ran (read from the stored result — no network, no cost), what its absence removes from the case, and the exact flag that runs it. Nothing here blocks or auto-spends: it reports. Tune `seed_policy` to change what counts as an exhausted seed; add a layer here when you add a collector, or it will never appear in the gap list.

layers._comment: One entry per evidence layer. `detect` is read against the stored pivot JSON: `enriched_with` matches a source name in meta.enriched_with, `meta` / `meta_any` test for a meta key, `result` for a top-level block, `archives` for an archive key, `pivot_prefix` for any pivot whose kind starts with that string, and `fetched` means the page itself was retrieved. `cost` is free | free_account | keyed | metered — the gap list is ordered so the FREE gaps come first, because those are the ones with no excuse. `applies_to` keeps an IP seed from being told it never ran the document-metadata layer. `without_it` is the analytic consequence, written for the assessment: it is the sentence that belongs in the report when the layer did not run.

fetch.label: page fetch / DOM
fetch.evidence: the page the operator actually served — every DOM-derived artifact depends on it
fetch.without_it: no page was retrieved, so every artifact in this result came from third parties; treat the collection as second-hand

whois.label: WHOIS / RDAP
whois.evidence: registrar, registration and expiry dates, nameservers, registrant when not proxied
whois.without_it: no registration timeline, so the case cannot place this domain in a batch or an era
whois.how: automatic on every domain (keyless RDAP + port-43 fallback)

crtsh.label: certificate transparency
crtsh.evidence: every name a CA has logged for this domain — subdomains the DNS never advertised
crtsh.without_it: the estate is only as big as the names we happened to be given

archive.label: Wayback / archive timeline
archive.evidence: what this host served BEFORE today — a site parked now may have been the live scam last year
archive.without_it: the host is judged on one moment in time, which is the moment the operator chose to leave up

liveness.label: liveness classification
liveness.evidence: whether the host still serves the operator's content, decided by READING the page rather than by its status code
liveness.without_it: a parking page or a default nginx page can be collected as though it were the operator's site, and its template artifacts clustered
liveness.how: domain_liveness <host>  (offline from a stored capture with case=)

paths.label: URL path / kit identifier
paths.evidence: the kit directory, which survives when the hostname is disposable and rotates weekly
paths.without_it: an operator who carries no information in the hostname has no clusterable artifact left
paths.how: automatic on a URL with a path; url_paths <url>

capture.label: raw evidence capture
capture.evidence: the bytes served — DOM plus every JS/CSS, each hashed, under one bundle digest
capture.without_it: every finding is an assertion about a page that will be gone in days, with nothing to re-check it against
capture.how: pivot_extract --case <id>  (capture is ON by default whenever --case is set)

passive_dns.label: passive DNS
passive_dns.evidence: historical name → IP, and the other names seen on those addresses
passive_dns.without_it: only today's resolution is known, so an origin the operator has since hidden behind a CDN stays hidden

passive_ssl.label: passive SSL (cert → IP history)
passive_ssl.evidence: every address observed serving this exact certificate over time — the ORIGIN-RECOVERY direction
passive_ssl.without_it: the box the operator served the certificate on before fronting it with a CDN is not recoverable
passive_ssl.how: same CIRCL credentials as passive DNS; passive_ssl origin <host>

urlscan.label: urlscan reverse
urlscan.evidence: reverse lookup by favicon hash and by the distinctive third-party resource — strong on fresh registrations
urlscan.without_it: the favicon and the kit's own script stop being reverse pivots; extract is not reverse

fofa.label: FOFA reverse
fofa.evidence: reverse by icon_hash, body content and IP — the widest of the reverse indexes
fofa.without_it: an artifact can be extracted but never turned into the estate that shares it
fofa.how: set FOFA_KEY (+ FOFA_EMAIL for the classic API)

censys.label: Censys certificate / host
censys.evidence: the certificate's own record and the hosts presenting it
censys.without_it: one corroboration path for a TLS-based link is missing; the CenQL query is still emitted for the UI
censys.how: censys cert <sha256>  — 100 credits a MONTH, per account; check `censys budget` first

intelx.label: Intelligence X — leaks, stealer logs, pastes, darknet
intelx.evidence: a corpus OUTSIDE the live internet: infostealer logs indexed by the URL the malware captured (victims, non-public panel URLs, sometimes the operator's own machine), breach rows that date an identity, historical WHOIS, and the phonebook inventory of a domain's emails and subdomains
intelx.without_it: the case has searched only what the operator is currently serving. This is the single most consequential absence in the list: an empty leak result is NOT a negative finding when the corpus was never queried

advertising.label: advertising + cloaking probe
advertising.evidence: what the operator PAID for — a Google-verified advertiser id and the legal entity funding it, the reverse to every other domain that account advertised, plus the FREE click-keyed cloaking probe
advertising.without_it: a paying identity that WHOIS privacy cannot hide is never looked for — and on a cloaked funnel the collection may be describing the decoy page rather than the scam
advertising.how: pivot_extract --serp --cloak-probe  (the cloaking probe alone is free and needs no key)

docmeta.label: document / image metadata
docmeta.evidence: author, XMP DocumentID, GPS and camera from the PDFs and images the site HOSTS — survives a re-skin
docmeta.without_it: an identity that outlives every rebrand is left unread. An empty result here is normal and is not a finding

screenshot.label: rendered screenshot
screenshot.evidence: what a victim saw, hashed and timestamped — the evidence a non-technical reader can actually judge
screenshot.without_it: the report describes a page nobody outside the team will ever see

impersonation.label: lookalike / typosquat hunt
impersonation.evidence: the registered lookalikes of the brand or of the seed itself, from CT plus DNS
impersonation.without_it: the estate is bounded by what was handed to us rather than by what the operator registered

sandbox.label: sandbox / TI lookup on the served file
sandbox.evidence: what the delivered sample DID when detonated — the runtime C2 a packed binary hides from static analysis
sandbox.without_it: a file the site serves is known only by its hash

seed_policy._comment: What counts as an exhausted seed. `required_layers` are the ones whose absence means the seed was TRIAGED, not worked — chosen because each is a distinct SEARCH SPACE rather than another view of the page we already have: the leak corpus, the historical resolution, the reverse index, and the raw capture that lets any of it be re-checked. `free_first` is the order to close gaps in when budget is a concern. A seed that fails the check is never blocked and never auto-collected: the point is that the assessment says which search it is drawn from.

reporting._comment: The sentences this layer must put in front of an analyst, phrased so that a gap cannot be read as a negative finding. The first one is the whole point of the file.
reporting.triage_note: SEED NOT EXHAUSTED — this was a TRIAGE. The layers below never ran, so their evidence classes were not searched at all. Do not report 'nothing further found' from a collection that did not look.
reporting.exhausted_note: Seed exhausted: every required evidence layer has run against this host.
reporting.absence_note: A layer that did not run produces no result. That is absence of COLLECTION, not absence of evidence.
reporting.keyless_note: Some gaps are closed by a credential rather than by a command; those are marked keyed/metered and cost money or quota.
